difficulty_why: Requesting full Gmail access (https://mail.google.com/) is a restricted scope requiring Google verification and an annual third-party CASA security assessment costing hundreds to thousands of dollars.

dev_time.label: 15-30 min
dev_time.text: Time to create a Google Cloud project, enable the Gmail API, configure the consent screen in Testing mode, and obtain client credentials for development testing.

launch_time.label: 4-8 weeks
launch_time.text: Time needed to prepare privacy documentation, complete domain verification, pass Google OAuth review, and obtain a Letter of Validation from a CASA security assessor.

own_app_reasons.label: Custom branding
own_app_reasons.text: Displays your own product name, logo, and support links on Google's consent screen instead of Composio.

own_app_reasons.label: Independent quota and rate limits
own_app_reasons.text: Avoids sharing daily API quota units and rate limits with other applications on Composio's shared credentials.

own_app_reasons.label: Enterprise domain control
own_app_reasons.text: Allows Google Workspace administrators to whitelist your specific client ID for internal organizational access without external review.

app_type.label: Web Application
app_type.text: OAuth 2.0 Client ID with application type 'Web application' and 'External' user type. Composio requires a web application client to handle server-side authorization code redirects, and external user type allows any standard Gmail user to connect.

prerequisites.label: Google Account and Cloud Project
prerequisites.text: A Google Account with access to create projects in Google Cloud Console.

prerequisites.label: Verified Domain in Search Console
prerequisites.text: Domain ownership verified in Google Search Console by a project owner or editor for all authorized domains.

prerequisites.label: Public Privacy Policy and Terms of Service
prerequisites.text: Publicly accessible Privacy Policy and Terms of Service hosted on the verified domain complying with Google API Services User Data Policy.

prerequisites.label: Demo Video for Verification
prerequisites.text: A YouTube video link demonstrating the end-to-end OAuth consent flow and how requested scopes are used in the app.

steps.label: Create Google Cloud Project
steps.text: Create a new project or select an existing project in the Google Cloud Console.

steps.label: Enable Gmail API
steps.text: In the API Library, search for 'Gmail API' and click 'Enable'.

steps.label: Configure OAuth Audience
steps.text: Navigate to Google Auth platform > Audience, select 'External' as the User Type, and click Save.

steps.label: Configure OAuth Branding
steps.text: Configure App name, User support email, Homepage, Privacy policy, Terms of service links, and Developer contact information.

steps.label: Add OAuth Scopes
steps.text: Under Data Access / Scopes, click 'Add or Remove Scopes' and select all required Google profile, contacts, and Gmail scopes.

steps.label: Create OAuth Client ID
steps.text: Under Clients, click 'Create Client', set Application type to 'Web application', set the Authorized redirect URI to https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, and click Create.

steps.label: Copy Client Credentials
steps.text: Copy the generated Client ID and Client Secret from the confirmation modal to enter into your Composio app settings.

steps.label: Submit for Verification
steps.text: Submit your OAuth consent screen for verification in Google Cloud Console to remove the 100 test user limit and unverified app warning.

fields.label: Scope justification
fields.value: <Explain how each scope is used by your agent>

approval.label: When required
approval.text: Required before public launch whenever an app requests sensitive scopes (such as contacts or profile read) or restricted scopes (such as https://mail.google.com/).

approval.label: What's checked
approval.text: Google verifies domain ownership via Search Console, privacy policy compliance with Limited Use requirements, written scope justifications, a YouTube demo video showing the consent flow, and a CASA security assessment for restricted scopes.

approval.label: Wait
approval.text: Full verification and third-party security assessment can take several weeks to several months depending on scope sensitivity and assessment tier.

approval.label: Cost
approval.text: Google charges no fee for verification, but third-party CASA security assessments from authorized assessors typically cost between $499 and $5,400 annually.

approval.label: Common rejections
approval.text: Failure to demonstrate user-facing features for each scope in the demo video, requesting broad scopes instead of narrower alternatives, or privacy policy non-compliance with Google Limited Use requirements.

approval.label: Before approval
approval.text: Unverified apps can only be accessed by up to 100 pre-registered test users and will display an unverified app warning screen during authorization.

pitfalls.label: Mandatory CASA Assessment
pitfalls.text: The scope https://mail.google.com/ is restricted and requires passing a third-party Cloud Application Security Assessment (CASA) before public release.

pitfalls.label: 100 Test User Cap in Testing Mode
pitfalls.text: While in 'Testing' mode, only explicitly invited Google test accounts (up to 100) can sign in; all other users receive an authorization error.

pitfalls.label: Domain Ownership Mismatch
pitfalls.text: Authorized domains must be verified in Google Search Console using the exact Google account that is an Owner or Editor of the Cloud project.

pitfalls.label: 7-Day Brand Publishing Window
pitfalls.text: Once branding verification succeeds, you must click 'Publish branding' within 7 days or status reverts to requiring re-verification.

pitfalls.label: Redirect URI Mismatch
pitfalls.text: The redirect URI in Google Cloud Console must match https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add character-for-character.

pitfalls.label: Annual Recertification Deadline
pitfalls.text: Restricted scope CASA assessments must be renewed annually with an updated Letter of Validation to maintain public access.

email_subject: Inquiry regarding OAuth App Verification and CASA Assessment for Gmail Integration ([Project ID])
email_body:
Hi Google Cloud OAuth Verification Support Team,

We are developing an AI agent application that allows users to connect their Gmail accounts to read and manage emails via OAuth 2.0.

Our app details:
- Project ID: [Your Google Cloud Project ID]
- Client ID: [Your Google Cloud OAuth Client ID]
- Intended Scopes: https://mail.google.com/, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.profile, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/contacts.readonly
- Redirect URI: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add

Could you please clarify:
1. What CASA assessment tier (Tier 2 self-scan vs. Tier 3 authorized lab audit) will be assigned for this use case?
2. Are there any prerequisites or specific phrasing needed in our Privacy Policy and demo video to minimize verification review turnaround?

Thank you,
[Your Name]
[Your Company/App Name]
[Your Contact Information]
